- Target start of production (private cluster) in Q4 2027
- Initial sustained throughput: ~1.2M tokens/day (inference) — rough guess => likely 4-6 H100 equiv nodes to start

Tom — thanks for the clear ask. We can put together a concise MAP and a sizing recommendation for the evaluation period vs committed pool. Quick thoughts before we produce the doc:

- We should run a 2-week eval with a 2-node H100 staging cluster to collect steady-state token/sec and tail latency. That will let us lock to a 4 vs 6 node committed posture.
- Lead times: off-the-shelf Dedicated (Redwood-managed) can be provisioned in 4-6 weeks once contract/commit signed; Private (customer-managed on-prem) including delivery & on-ramp typically requires 10-14 weeks for procurement + 4-6 weeks for on-prem integration depending on rack/network readiness. Marissa / infra can add specifics.
- Compliance: we’ll attach a SOC2 summary and proposed data flow diagram.

Ben / Tom — adding technical detail from the infra team so procurement has something concrete:

- GPU sizing: if you’re hitting ~1.2M tokens/day with average 32-token responses, estimate ~40k tokens/hour peak. Conservative start: 4 H100S A100-sized nodes (we typically quote as H100-equivalent instances) — warms to 6 nodes as steady growth headroom. Final number dependent on prompt lengths and batching.
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed hosted machines): 4–6 weeks after signed SOW to reserve and route capacity (includes scheduling, image bake, and placement).
- Private (VPC / on-prem): 12–16 weeks typical for customers who need hardware procurement (H100 availability varies by region). On-prem integration adds 3–4 weeks for rack, networking and test harness.
- Acceptance criteria: we propose 72-hour production-like soak at the committed throughput with <150ms p50 token latency target and <1.5x p90 multiplier during peak.

I’ve attached a short SOC2 extract (SOC2-Redwood-summary.pdf) and updated the MAP sheet with the technical milestones.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Infrastructure Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Tom — procurement/finance note:

- Pricing: we can offer a staged commitment with a 3-month evaluation credit for the 2-node eval cluster. Post-eval, the committed tranche pricing would lock for 12 months.
- Fallback: to avoid production gaps, we recommend a hybrid runway — keep a modest hosted buffer (burst capacity) for 6 weeks post-commit while private Dedicated gear is arriving. We’ll include explicit fallback rules in the MAP (automatic routing to compatible model variant and region if tranche unavailable).
- Legal: procurement wants a timeline that ties milestones to invoicing triggers. I’ll draft language that maps milestones (eval complete, PO issuance, hardware delivery, acceptance) to payment schedule.
